# `raptorbt.adapters`

Broker adapters: the common layer, a conformance kit and thin mappings.

``BrokerAdapter`` is the base every broker mapping builds on
(``raptorbt.adapters.kite``, ``.upstox``, ``.dhan``). ``raptorbt.adapters.conformance``
tests any execution adapter, including your own. Guide:
``docs/architecture/broker-adapters.md``.

### `BrokerAdapter`

*class*

```python
class BrokerAdapter
BrokerAdapter(session: 'Session', instruments: 'Mapping[str, Instrument] | Callable[[str], Instrument | None]', *, executor: 'Executor | None' = None, limiter: 'RateLimiter | None' = None, backoff: 'Backoff | None' = None, sleep: 'Callable[[float], None]' = <built-in function sleep>, clock_ns: 'Callable[[], int]' = <function _clock_ns>, max_attempts: 'int' = 4, resend_if_absent: 'bool' = False, resend_delay: 'float' = 2.0, default_product: 'str' = 'intraday', reduce_only: 'str' = 'refuse', gtc: 'str' = 'refuse', namespace: 'str', account_id: 'str | None' = None, fill_source: 'str | None' = None, verifier: 'Callable[[Any], bool] | None' = None, trusted: 'bool' = False, retention_s: 'float | None' = 3600.0, monotonic: 'Callable[[], float]' = <built-in function monotonic>, lease: 'Callable[[int], bool] | Any | None' = None) -> 'None'
```

Base of the broker mappings. See the module docs; subclasses fill the hooks.

``lease`` (default ``None``): the host's proof that this process may still send for the
current epoch, ``callable(epoch) -> bool`` or an object with ``holds(epoch)``. It is consulted
before every outbound write (submit, cancel, modify and their retries). A ``False`` answer, or
an exception, fails closed: the write is refused with :class:`Fenced`, queued writes are
dropped (``fenced_drop`` events) and nothing more is sent until ``fence()`` is called with a
higher epoch. Without a lease ``can_fence`` is ``False`` and ``fence()`` guards only this process.

``gtc`` (default ``"refuse"``): the venues here have no good-till-cancelled
order, so ``gtc`` orders (the engine's default) are ``Unsupported`` unless
``gtc="day"`` sends them as day orders.

Hooks a mapping implements: ``translate``, ``check_modify``, ``place``,
``cancel_remote``, ``modify_remote``, ``fetch_orders``, ``fetch_positions``,
``fetch_balances``, ``parse_order_update`` and optionally ``find_by_tag``.

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `add_instrument(self, symbol: 'str', spec: 'Any' = None) -> 'None'` | A node added ``symbol`` (its :class:`~raptorbt.InstrumentSpec` is ``spec``): learn how the broker names it, so orders for it can be sent. Looks in ``instruments`` first, then asks :meth:`resolve_instrument`; raises :class:`Unsupported` when neither knows it, which makes the node refuse the add. Idempotent: a restored node replays it. |
| `balances(self) -> 'VenueBalances'` | *No docstring.* |
| `can_fence` | True only when the host gave a ``lease``: fencing then holds across processes. |
| `cancel(self, client_order_id: 'str') -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `cancel_exit_rule(self, request: 'Any') -> 'None'` | Take back an exit rule :meth:`place_exit_rule` accepted (``request`` is the one that was placed). Return when the venue no longer holds it; raise ``Unsupported`` when it cannot be taken back, and the engine will not report the rule cancelled. |
| `cancel_remote(self, rec: '_Rec') -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `catch_up(self) -> 'list[QueuedReport]'` | Read the venue's order book (and its trades, for ``fill_source="trades"``) now and return the reports of everything the node has not heard: a fill, a cancel or a rejection that happened while no node was listening. Blocking: call it from the node's thread before it compares itself with the venue (``LiveNode.reconcile`` does). |
| `check_modify(self, rec: '_Rec', quantity: 'float | None', limit_price: 'float | None', trigger_price: 'float | None') -> 'None'` | Pure: raise ``Unsupported`` if the broker cannot make this change. |
| `close(self) -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `connection_lost(self, reason: 'str' = '') -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `connection_restored(self) -> 'None'` | The feed is back: read the order book, since messages may have been missed. |
| `default_limiter(self, sleep: 'Callable[[float], None]') -> 'RateLimiter'` | *No docstring.* |
| `deliver_to(self, node: 'Any') -> 'list[str]'` | Drain the queue into ``node.push_report`` (call on the node's thread, never from inside an adapter method). |
| `drain_events(self) -> 'list[AdapterEvent]'` | *No docstring.* |

### `Executor`

*class*

```python
class Executor(Protocol)
Executor(*args, **kwargs)
```

What an adapter needs from whoever runs its broker calls.

``bind(pump)`` hands over the adapter's drain function once; ``kick()`` says the outbox has work and
must not block on I/O; ``close()`` stops whatever the executor started. ``InlineExecutor``,
``ManualExecutor`` and ``ThreadExecutor`` are the three provided. An executor that runs a
thread may also have ``health()``, a dict the adapter's ``health()`` carries.

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `bind(self, pump: 'Callable[[], int]') -> 'None'` | Called once with the adapter's ``pump``. |
| `close(self) -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `kick(self) -> 'None'` | There is work in the outbox. Must not block on I/O. |

Encode a client order id to a broker tag and back.

``charset`` is a regex class body of the characters the broker allows

### `OrderStatusUpdate`

*class*

```python
class OrderStatusUpdate
OrderStatusUpdate(venue_order_id: 'str', status: 'str', client_order_id: 'str | None' = None, tag: 'str | None' = None, symbol: 'str | None' = None, side: 'str | None' = None, order_type: 'str | None' = None, product: 'str | None' = None, quantity: 'float | None' = None, filled_qty: 'float' = 0.0, avg_price: 'float | None' = None, limit_price: 'float | None' = None, trigger_price: 'float | None' = None, reason: 'str | None' = None, ts_ns: 'int' = 0, cancel_failed: 'bool' = False, modify_failed: 'bool' = False) -> None
```

One broker order row, normalised: a feed message or a row of the order book.

``filled_qty`` is cumulative and ``avg_price`` the average over it. A mapping builds its rows
with the broker's own count (lots for an instrument declared ``quantity_in_lots``); the base
converts every inbound row once, so rows seen through ``orders()``, ``open_orders()`` and
``handle_update`` are always in **units** (prices are per unit).

### `RateLimiter`

*class*

```python
class RateLimiter
RateLimiter(classes: 'Mapping[str, Iterable[TokenBucket]]', *, sleep: 'Callable[[float], None]' = <built-in function sleep>) -> 'None'
```

Endpoint classes, each with one or more windows (per second, per minute...).

A request waits until every window of its class has a token. The wait is in
the caller's thread, which for an adapter is the executor, never the node.

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `acquire(self, klass: 'str') -> 'float'` | Block until a request of ``klass`` may go. Returns the seconds waited. |
| `per_window(cls, spec: 'Mapping[str, Iterable[tuple[int, float]]]', *, clock: 'Callable[[], float]' = <built-in function monotonic>, sleep: 'Callable[[float], None]' = <built-in function sleep>) -> 'RateLimiter'` | ``{"orders": [(10, 1), (400, 60)]}``: 10 a second and 400 a minute. |

### `Session`

*class*

```python
class Session
Session(token: 'str | Secret', *, refresh: 'Callable[[], str] | None' = None, api_key: 'str | Secret | None' = None) -> 'None'
```

What the caller gives the adapter to authenticate: a token and, optionally,
a way to get a new one.

``refresh`` is the caller's own login (it holds the credentials, TOTP seed
and so on; the adapter never sees them) and returns a new token. When a
call comes back unauthorised the adapter calls it once and retries; with no
``refresh`` the outbox pauses and a ``session_expired`` event is raised
until the host calls ``adapter.set_token``. Note that a new login on some
brokers revokes the previous token everywhere: refresh from one place only.

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `api_key(self) -> 'str | None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `token(self) -> 'str'` | *No docstring.* |
| `update(self, token: 'str | Secret') -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |

### `ThreadExecutor`

*class*

```python
class ThreadExecutor
ThreadExecutor(name: 'str' = 'raptorbt-adapter') -> 'None'
```

One daemon worker thread drains the outbox in order.

One thread keeps the order of a venue's requests (a cancel never overtakes
its submit). Rate-limit waits and retry sleeps happen on it, never on the
node's thread.

| --- | --- |

| `close(self) -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |
| `health(self) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` | Whether the worker is running and what, if anything, made a drain fail. |
| `kick(self) -> 'None'` | *No docstring.* |

### `VenueBalances`

*class*

```python
class VenueBalances
VenueBalances(available: 'float', currency: 'str', used: 'float | None' = None, total: 'float | None' = None) -> None
```

Money at the venue, in ``currency`` (always named: the mapping knows its venue's).

``available`` can be used for new orders now; ``used`` is margin or funds already committed and
``total`` the account's whole balance, both ``None`` when the broker does not say. Amounts are
positive money in the currency's main unit (rupees, not paise); a shortfall shows as a small or
zero ``available``, never a negative ``used``.

### `VenueOrder`

*class*

```python
class VenueOrder
VenueOrder(venue_order_id: 'str', status: 'str', client_order_id: 'str | None' = None, tag: 'str | None' = None, symbol: 'str | None' = None, side: 'str | None' = None, order_type: 'str | None' = None, product: 'str | None' = None, quantity: 'float | None' = None, filled_qty: 'float' = 0.0, avg_price: 'float | None' = None, limit_price: 'float | None' = None, trigger_price: 'float | None' = None, reason: 'str | None' = None, ts_ns: 'int' = 0, cancel_failed: 'bool' = False, modify_failed: 'bool' = False) -> None
```

One broker order row, normalised: a feed message or a row of the order book.

``filled_qty`` is cumulative and ``avg_price`` the average over it. A mapping builds its rows
with the broker's own count (lots for an instrument declared ``quantity_in_lots``); the base
converts every inbound row once, so rows seen through ``orders()``, ``open_orders()`` and
``handle_update`` are always in **units** (prices are per unit).

broker's lot count), and signed: long positive, short negative, flat rows are not listed.
``avg_price`` is per unit and positive.

### `new_namespace`

*function*

```python
new_namespace(length: 'int' = 4) -> 'str'
```

A fresh per-run tag prefix from the operating system's random source.

Client ids restart at ``s0-0`` every run, so tags from two runs of a node
(or two nodes on one account) would collide without it. Generate one at
each start; keep it in the saved state so a recovered run keeps its own.

### `reconnect_loop`

*function*

```python
reconnect_loop(connect: 'Callable[[], None]', *, backoff: 'Backoff | None' = None, sleep: 'Callable[[float], None]' = <built-in function sleep>, should_stop: 'Callable[[], bool]' = <function <lambda>>, on_connected: 'Callable[[], None] | None' = None, on_lost: 'Callable[[BaseException], None] | None' = None, stable_after: 'float' = 10.0, clock: 'Callable[[], float]' = <built-in function monotonic>) -> 'None'
```

Run ``connect`` (which blocks while the connection lives) until stopped.

After every loss, wait the backoff and connect again; the backoff starts over
once a connection has lasted ``stable_after`` seconds. Wire ``on_lost`` to
``adapter.connection_lost`` and ``on_connected`` to
``adapter.connection_restored``, so the adapter reads the venue's order book
after any gap.
